payload.query: Under OC 186A, are PoS tap payments for merchants or person-to-person transfers?

claims.text: Under OC 186A, UPI Tap & Pay on Point of Sale (PoS) terminals is restricted to Person-to-Merchant transactions.

reasons: The claim is fully supported by the provided excerpt which explicitly states that UPI Tap & Pay transactions on PoS terminals are accepted only for Person-to-Merchant (P2M) transactions.

quotes.quote: Key Guidelines 1. Members and UPI Application Providers shall ensure that UPI Tap & Pay transactions on PoS terminals are accepted only for Person-to-Merchant (P2M) transactions.

sources.text: serena a Oe Prt | FORWPRD NPCI/UPI/OC-186A/2026-27 10" September 2026 To, Members and UPI Application Providers — Unified Payments Interface (UPI) Subject: Enhancement - UPI Tap & Pay on Point of Sale (PoS) With reference to UPI Operating Circular NPCI/UPI/OC-186/2023-24 dated 19° December 2023, UPI Tap & Pay through Near Field Communication (NFC) on QR was introduced as an additional mode for initiating UPI transactions. In addition to QR, UPI Tap & Pay shall now be extended to Point of Sale (PoS) terminals enabling Users to make contactless (NFC-based) UPI! payments by unlocking their mobile device and tapping it on the PoS terminal.
sources.title: Enhancement - UPI Tap & Pay on Point of Sale (PoS)

sources.text: Key Guidelines 1. Members and UPI Application Providers shall ensure that UPI Tap & Pay transactions on PoS terminals are accepted only for Person-to-Merchant (P2M) transactions.
sources.title: Enhancement - UPI Tap & Pay on Point of Sale (PoS)

sources.text: 4. Members and UPI Application Providers shall ensure that settlement, reconciliation, dispute management, and Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) for UPI Tap & Pay transactions are carried out in accordance with the extant UPI guidelines as per applicability.
sources.title: Enhancement - UPI Tap & Pay on Point of Sale (PoS)

sources.text: 3. Members and UPI Application Providers shall ensure that per transaction limit is capped at ₹5000, up to which additional factor of authentication shall not be required.

sources.text: With India heading towards a digital future and BHIM UPI assisting in its growth by taking a progressive initiative to take the country to a “less cash society”. The Tricolor arrows, created by combining the fast-forward symbol with our National flag and taking inspiration from the stance of an athlete, visually captures this statement. Capturing the same elements from the official NPCI logo, the sharp edges of the arrows in the symbol point towards the future, reflecting UPI’s accelerated commitment to the country’s progress, while the curved edges negate the frivolousness, brilliantly juxtaposing BHIM UPI’s zorward-thinking with its nationalistic and traditional values. The BHIM UPI and Fast-Forward mnemonics are the copyrighted and trademarked properties of NPCI. No part of the mnemonics or artwork may be reproduced by any means or in any form whatsoever without written permission.
sources.title: OC - 100 Mandatory Brand Guidelines for BHIM UPI

sources.text: NPC NATIONALPAYMENTSCORPORATIONOFINDIA NPC1/UPI/OC-99/2020-21 12thJanuary,2021 To, AllMembersparticipatinginvariousNPCIProducts Madam/DearSir, Sub:AdherencetoNPClguidelinesbymembers/participants adherence to various guidelines of NPCI by the members/participants for all NPC Products. It is also in the interest of the eco-system that the members/participants observe the rules and regulations set by NPCl through Procedural Guidelines (PG) and Operating Circulars (OC) to ensure that the eco-system runs on the same standards and principles of integrity and credibility. With the continuous evolution and increased pace of development of payment landscape in the country including theparticipants leveraging thetechnological developments,and alsothe requirement to ensure safe, secure and efficient payment systems, it is incumbent on all participants to ensure strict adherence ofthevariousNPCIguidelines. NPCl shall ensure that the members/participants are adhering to PGs and OCs of all products of NPCl. Though such activity are presently monitored/tracked at our end and raised to participant concerned when issues are observed,there is noformal process of recording members/participants self-attestation confirming adherence to all NPCl guidelines and take corrective measures/actions for cases where continuous non-adherence is observed. Also, it becomes quite difficult to track the status and progress or the customer need hardly be emphasized here. To address this gap, we are implementing the process of obtaining a self-attestation from members that they are complying with the NPCl guidelines.We attach herewith the AnnexureAwhichcoversresponsibilitiesofmembers/participants and AnnexureB which covers NPCl guidelines to be adhered

sources.text: 1001A, B wing, 10th Floor, The Capital, Bandra-Kurla Complex, Bandra (East), Mumbai - 400 051 CIN: U74990MH2008NPL189067 NPCI/UPI/OC No. 28 Date: August 18, 2017 To, All member banks – Unified Payment Interface (UPI), SUB: Scanning UPI credentials integrated in Bharat QR through UPI PSP Application This bears reference to the NPCI circular: NPCI /2017-18/PD/004 dated on August 10th, 2017 about “Integration of Bharat QR with UPI credential” and emphasizes on compliance with Merchant QR code specification V4.0 and ensuring that all Bharat QR deployed post 15th Sept, 2017 should contain UPI credentials. With the introduction of above, All UPI PSP applications should be able to scan & pay using both UPI QR as well as Bharat QR (integrated with UPI credentials). Further in this regards, NPCI had sent communication to all the UPI PSPs and had released the technical specification (Annexure of UPI linking Spec for Bharat QR_V1.5.2) to scan/read UPI credentials from Bharat QRs to all the UPI member banks. Therefore we request to all the UPI member banks to comply with UPI linking specs for Bharat QR_V1.5.2 and do the necessary development in their PSP applications for reading / scanning Bharat QRs. Please ensure all PSP applications are equipped to read both UPI QR as well as Bharat QR by 15th Sept, 2017. Please acknowledge the receipt of
sources.title: Circular 28 – Scanning UPI credential integrated in Bharat QR through UPI

sources.text: fs Conroe =) NPCI/UPI/OC no.199/2024-25 25" June 2024 To, All Members, UPI (Unified Payment Interface) Dear Sir/Madam, Subject: Update to NPCI CL version 1.8 or above UPI has become a preferred digital payment mode across the country. It provides ease of use, convenience and superior user experience with security and interoperability. To ensure the safety and security of the UPI systems, NPCI constantly reviews the security checks of all components in the UPI ecosystem and regularly upgrades them to address evolving threats in cyber landscape. There are security checks implemented as part of the code embedded in the Common Library (CL) along with the feature release to enhance user experience on UPI platforms. Integration of latest versions of CL is important to ensure enhanced security and safety in UPI ecosystem. With this objective, NPCI will be retiring the support for CL prior to Version 1.8 after 30% September 2024. To ensure compliance PSP Banks shall certify and enable CL 1.8 or above and their respective UPI Apps shall integrate the latest version of CL within their application, on or before 30% September 2024. Members are requested to take note of this compliance and communicate it to relevant stakeholders and their respective partners. Yours sincerely, SD/- Kunal Kalawatia Chief of Products 1001A, The Capital, B Wing, 10* Floor, Bandra Kurla Complex,
sources.title: Update to NPCI CL version 1.8 or above
